messages.content: Solve the programming-by-example task carefully. Compare only the two candidate predicate behaviors. Infer the shared mapper and predicate from the raw examples, then return the single more compatible choice.

Fixed skeleton: foldr((item,acc) => if predicate(item) then mapper(item)::acc else acc, [], xs). Raw examples: [] -> []; [-3,-1,0,2,4] -> [1,0,4]; [3,1,-2,4,2] -> [1,4]; [0,4,-1,3] -> [0,1]; [2,-3,1,-2] -> [4,1]. The mapper is one deterministic small arithmetic expression shared by every retained item. Domain order is [-3,-2,-1,0,1,2,3,4]. Choice A keep mask: 00111100. Choice B keep mask: 00011100. In a keep mask, 1 means retain that domain value and 0 means drop it. Which choice is more compatible with all examples?
